paper_title: The Tape Reconfiguration Problem and Its Consequences for Dominating Set Reconfiguration
classifications: Theory of computation → Finite Model Theory
Theory of computation → Parameterized complexity and exact algorithms
statement: We were not able to determine if the problem is XL-complete or not and leave as an open problem the exact complexity of Path-Tape-Rec.
context: The W-hierarchy can be generalized to higher levels; W[h] problems can be expressed in the same way except that up to h nested boolean operators are allowed. Therefore, in order to prove that Multi-Tape-Rec is W[h]-hard, we build on this W[2]-hardness result and design OR gadgets and AND gadgets allowing us to lift W[h + 1]-hardness from W[h]-hardness. Note that this has to be done without adding too many characters nor additional tapes. The details of the proof can be found in the full version of the paper. We were not able to determine if the problem is XL-complete or not and leave as an open problem the exact complexity of Path-Tape-Rec.
